judgements.justification: B's reviewers knew single-agent offline RL, caught the under-run CQL baseline and tied the method to EMaQ, BRAC and KL-control; A's reviewers, at confidence 2 or 3, probed derivations and notation and praised the single-agent results.
B's AC said some reviewers were 'not fully convinced', which matches 5dG2's and Rr7B's final comments; no final position was misstated.
No reviewer or AC in either committee raised a narrow-audience or wrong-venue concern.
A had no low-scoring detractor, and B's AC rejected rather than argued for acceptance.
Both committees saw the expanded D4RL table and the MMM sweep; the CQL concession on B's forum did not raise B above A (R04 covers it).
B's only confidence-5 reviewer, xr9t, was thin (2 hours) and the AC followed 5dG2 and its own re-review judgement, not a mean that overrode an expert.
All objections and score changes in both committees came during the discussion, and the authors answered them.
B's reviewers' text was more critical (mixed results, copied baselines, limited novelty), so the rating gap reflects different judgements, not scoring leniency.

B's Rr7B judged the offline multi-agent framing overstated for a method that is single-agent at heart, the authors offered to retitle, and B's AC required those edits to be re-reviewed; A took the framing at face value.
A's low-confidence reviewers settled on 7, not the marginal-accept 6, and A's AC lifted them to a spotlight rather than reading them as poster-level.
